Our five miles course was used and Joe Flower won from A. Kench, who was running for Old Emanuel A.C., and is, of course, a members of our Club.
Joe Flower carried on the good work, overhauling the Highgate and Tipton representatives and bringing us up to third position. Joe's run was a very fine one and a Club record for this stage.

The S.L.H. representative passed our man, Joe Flower, on the next stage and this remained our position to the end, Jim Tosh running last. Thus we gained seven points during the afternoon, which consolidated our position in the League.

Robbins, the S.L.H. runner, won the Mile for Slough H. in fine style, with Joe Flower and Norman Dewberry scoring for us. Somebody said our mile Champion started in this race, but at all events he was missing at the finish, so we make this statement with reserve.

Joe Flower's son writes to inform us of his father's recent death. Joe was one of our leading runners in the twenties and thirties and was a former one mile Club Champion.

Joe Flower, writing from West Africa, says of 'The Belgravian' ``What pleasure that little journal brings''. Dan Patience, after having been stationed in the wilds of Ayr, bemoaning his fate because he couldn't get a run, now writes from North Africa!
